2024_193_m011624org_regbdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education organizational and regular meeting held January 16, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Schmidt and adjourned at 7:55 p.m. The Board re-elected Schmidt president, Anne vice president, and Hauff secretary through December 31, 2024, appointed Assistant Superintendent Rick L. West as Treasurer, and adopted the 2024 meeting schedule, committee memberships, depository resolution, and legal counsel designations. The largest action was the award of high school athletic complex renovation bids totaling $13,005,160.00, alongside playground equipment awards totaling $2,692,774.60 and flooring work totaling $550,175.00.
2024_193_m011624org_regbdmtg.page:
Meeting and Attendance
Troy Board of Education organizational meeting and regular meeting, January 16, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Board members present: Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, Schmidt, and Wilson. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, and West. Four high school student representatives and approximately 25 audience members attended. Adjourned at 7:55 p.m.

Organizational Actions
Schmidt served as acting chairperson (7-0) and appointed Judy Holmes temporary secretary. By roll call, all seven members voted yes to elect Schmidt president, Anne vice president, and Hauff secretary, each until December 31, 2024. Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, was appointed Treasurer for the period January through December 2024 (7-0).

Annual Designations
| Item | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Depositories | Bank of America, Citizens Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Huntington Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), PNC Bank |
| Legal counsel (2024) | Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Miller Johnson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; Miller Canfield |
| Deputy Secretary | Superintendent of Schools, 2024 calendar year |
| Posting of meeting notices | Judy Holmes, Secretary to the Superintendent of Schools |
| Meeting schedule / committees | 2024 calendar and Board Committee Memberships adopted as attached |

The depository resolution authorizes withdrawal by facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West, and in emergencies the handwritten signature of West or Superintendent Richard M. Machesky on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America; PNC Bank accounts for Troy Career Center expenses require the handwritten signature of the Troy Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager, or Program Coordinators. Investments follow Board Policy 5000.06 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. Certified by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, this 17th day of January 2024.

Recognition and Public Comment
The TSD Mission Moment (SSAB Executive Board), Student Spotlight, and Board Recognition Month items were moved to the February 27, 2024 meeting because school was cancelled that day; Dr. Machesky informally recognized the Board and presented a gift of appreciation. Jeff Zendler, Troy resident and parent of four District students, asked whether new elementary playgrounds will be accessible and inclusive for students with disabilities. Jason Cichowicz, President of the Troy Education Association, addressed the Board about the TEA contract expiring January 31, 2024.

Consent Agenda and Personnel
Items A through E approved 7-0: minutes of the December 5, 2023 Special Meeting, December 5, 2023 Closed Session, December 5, 2023 Workshop, and December 12, 2023 Board Meeting, plus the November 2023 Treasurer's Report. Personnel recommendations for Jennifer Maxwell and Mallory Lyons approved 7-0. No curriculum items.

Fiber maintenance services were awarded to Fiber Link, Inc. consistent with its proposal to Bid #2324-05, as a General Fund expenditure (7-0). All business items passed 7-0.

Closing
Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, February 6th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building and the next Board Meeting for Tuesday, February 27th at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.
2024_193_m011624org_regbdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held January 16, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The document combines the Board's annual organizational meeting with the regular business meeting that followed.

ATTENDANCE AND CALL TO ORDER
President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, and West. Four high school student representatives attended along with approximately 25 members of the audience.

ELECTION OF ACTING CHAIRPERSON AND TEMPORARY SECRETARY
Mr. Schmidt explained that the evening's meeting is where the Board selects officers, appoints committee members for the upcoming year, and approves or authorizes items that must be considered on an annual basis, with the regular Board meeting to follow the organizational portion. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Alic that Mr. Schmidt serve as acting chairperson to officiate the meeting until the election of a president was completed; the vote was Yes 7, No 0. Mr. Schmidt appointed Judy Holmes to act as temporary secretary until the secretary of the Troy Board of Education was elected.

NOMINATION AND ELECTION OF PRESIDENT
Acting Chairperson Schmidt declared nominations in order for the office of Board president. Mrs. Alic nominated Mr. Schmidt. A motion by Ms. Schmidt, supported by Dr. Wilson, closed nominations for president (Yes 7, No 0). It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Wilson that Mr. Schmidt serve as president of the Troy Board of Education until December 31, 2024. On roll call: Alic - Yes, Anne - Yes, Hauff - Yes, Haupt - Yes, Philippart - Yes, Schmidt - Yes, Wilson - Yes.

NOMINATION AND ELECTION OF VICE PRESIDENT
President Schmidt declared nominations in order for vice president. Dr. Wilson nominated Mrs. Anne. A motion by Mr. Schmidt, supported by Mrs. Alic, closed nominations (Yes 7, No 0). It was moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Mrs. Alic that Mrs. Anne serve as vice president of the Troy Board of Education until December 31, 2024. On roll call: Anne - Yes, Hauff - Yes, Haupt - Yes, Schmidt - Yes, Wilson - Yes, Philippart - Yes, Alic - Yes.

NOMINATION AND ELECTION OF SECRETARY
President Schmidt declared nominations in order for Board secretary. Dr. Wilson nominated Mr. Hauff. A motion by Mr. Schmidt, supported by Mrs. Alic, closed nominations (Yes 7, No 0). It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Alic that Mr. Hauff serve as secretary of the Troy Board of Education until December 31, 2024. On roll call: Hauff - Yes, Haupt - Yes, Philippart - Yes, Schmidt - Yes, Wilson - Yes, Alic - Yes, Anne - Yes.

APPOINTMENT OF SCHOOL BOARD TREASURER
It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, be appointed Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education for the period January through December 2024. Yes 7, No 0.

FUND DEPOSITORIES AND INVESTMENTS
Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Dr. Wilson, the resolution recites that public monies belonging to or held for the State, County, or other political units of the State may come into the hands of Rick West, Treasurer of Troy School District, and that Michigan law requires the Board to provide by resolution for the deposit of all public monies including tax monies. The Treasurer is directed to deposit and/or invest all public monies in his name as Treasurer into the following depository institutions: Bank of America; Citizens Bank; JP Morgan Chase Bank; Comerica Bank; Huntington Bank; Fifth Third Bank; Flagstar Bancorp; MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank); and PNC Bank. Monies may be withdrawn by checks signed with a facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West, and in emergencies by the handwritten signature of Rick West or Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, who may sign on the General Fund account and the Payroll account at Bank of America. Accounts established at PNC Bank for paying Troy Career Center expenses may be drawn on by checks with the handwritten signature of the Troy Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager, or Program Coordinators. The Treasurer may open or close accounts with the listed institutions when in the District's interest. District funds may be invested according to Board Policy 5000.06, and the Treasurer is authorized to combine money from more than one fund for the purpose of making an investment authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. The maximum amount to be invested with the above institutions is regulated by the school code. The certification reads: "I, Gary Hauff, Secretary of Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, certify that the Resolution was adopted by said Board at a meeting thereof held on the date specified above," given under hand and seal of the Troy School District in the County of Oakland in the State of Michigan this 17th day of January 2024. Yes 7, No 0.

DESIGNATION OF BOARD AND DISTRICT LEGAL COUNSEL
Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic to continue the designation of Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Miller Johnson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Miller Canfield as legal counsel to advise and/or represent the Troy School District and Board of Education as necessary for the 2024 calendar year. The superintendent is authorized to consult additional counsel as needed with prior notification to the Board. Yes 7, No 0.

DESIGNATION OF SUPERINTENDENT AS DEPUTY SECRETARY
Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mr. Hauff to continue the designation of the Superintendent of Schools as Deputy Secretary of the Board with authority to act for the secretary for the 2024 calendar year. Yes 7, No 0.

DESIGNATION OF PERSON FOR POSTING NOTICES OF MEETINGS
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the person designated for posting notices of meetings for the 2024 calendar year shall be Judy Holmes, Secretary to the Superintendent of Schools. Yes 7, No 0.

MEETING SCHEDULE AND COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education adopt the schedule of meetings for the 2024 calendar year as indicated on the attached calendar. Yes 7, No 0. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Hauff that the Board adopt the Board Committee Memberships for the 2024 school year as attached. Yes 7, No 0.

RECOGNITION
President Schmidt announced that the TSD Mission Moment featuring the SSAB Executive Board, the Student Spotlight, and the Board Recognition Month item were all moved to the February 27, 2024 Board of Education Meeting due to the cancellation of school that day. Dr. Machesky nonetheless informally recognized the Board, thanked members for all they do for students and the community, and presented them with a gift of appreciation.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS
None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (FIRST)
Mr. Jeff Zendler, Troy resident and parent of four students in the District, addressed the Board about the new playgrounds being designed for elementary schools and whether they will be accessible and inclusive for all students, including students with disabilities.

CONSENT AGENDA
Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board approve items A, B, C, D, and E: minutes of the December 5, 2023 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the December 5, 2023 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the December 5, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the December 12, 2023 Board of Education Meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for November 2023. Yes 7, No 0.

PERSONNEL (ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY)
Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Board approve the personnel recommendations as stated, naming Jennifer Maxwell and Mallory Lyons. Yes 7, No 0.

CURRICULUM
None.

BUSINESS - FLOORING REPLACEMENT AND POLISHING PROJECT
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Wilson that the bid for flooring replacement work be awarded as follows and approved as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund: Shock Bros Floorcovering, flooring demo/replacement, $494,175.00; Diamond Shine Concrete & Stone, floor polishing, $26,000.00; Additional/Emergency Flooring, $30,000.00; TOTAL $550,175.00. Yes 7, No 0.

BUSINESS - PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT PURCHASE
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt that the bid for playground equipment and installation be awarded as follows and approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund: Sinclair Recreation/GameTime playground equipment, Contractor #1, $1,508,996.70; Midstate Recreation/Playworld playground equipment, Contractor #2, $1,183,777.90; TOTAL $2,692,774.60. Yes 7, No 0. Board members asked whether the playgrounds will be fully ADA compliant, especially for students with disabilities; Ms. Griffor indicated they have all been designed in alignment with ADA requirements.

BUSINESS - ATHLETIC COMPLEX UPGRADE
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Philippart that the bid for the high school athletic renovations be awarded as follows and approved as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund and the 2023 Capital Projects Fund: Cortis Bros Trucking & Excavating, site work, $8,505,700.00; City Contracting Services, architectural, $518,000.00; Contrast Mechanical, Inc., mechanical, $182,000.00; Innovated Energy Controls, electrical, $543,810.00; Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions, Inc., synthetic turf, $2,292,305.00; Contingency (8%), $963,345.00; TOTAL $13,005,160.00. Yes 7, No 0. Board members inquired about past flooding issues with baseball fields and whether the upgrade will address that problem; Mr. West indicated the upgrade will fix several major problems.

BUSINESS - FIBER MAINTENANCE
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Hauff that fiber maintenance services be awarded to Fiber Link, Inc. consistent with its submitted proposal to Bid #2324-05, with related expenditures approved as an expenditure of the General Fund. Yes 7, No 0.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (SECOND)
Mr. Jason Cichowicz, President of the Troy Education Association, addressed the Board about the TEA contract, which expires on January 31, 2024. He stated that working without a contract causes anxiety and frustration and that teachers feel disrespected, that many teachers are leaving the profession and choosing careers in surrounding districts, and that the association is ready to bargain and has offered many dates to negotiate.

OTHER
None.

BOARD COMMENTS
Dr. Wilson shared that the MLK Day event recognition for SSAB students will be held next month and gave a shout out to the students who worked at pulling it together; she also shared her excitement about the Student Equity Council kickoff and the way students are leading that work. Dr. Machesky thanked all the students and community members who came out to make the MLK Day event a success, noting several dignitaries attended and saw a showcase of service to the community. Mr. Schmidt announced that the next Board Workshop will be held Tuesday, February 6th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building and the next Board Meeting Tuesday, February 27th at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building.

ADJOURNMENT
The meeting was adjourned at 7:55 p.m. Respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (transcription notation GNH/jh).
